comments.body:
**Verification complete; one minor typo fixed.**

I audited the entire solution (literal reading) both symbolically (sympy) and numerically; the mathematics is fully correct.

1. **Lemma 1 (reduction):** (y+x/y)x=n with y=10-x multiplies (reversibly, y>0) to xy^2+x^2=ny, expanding to P_n(x)=x^3-19x^2+(n+100)x-10n=0, and n=g(x)=x(x^2-19x+100)/(10-x). Verified exactly (diff=0).

2. **Lemma 2 (monotone bijection):** g'(x)=(-2x^3+49x^2-380x+1000)/(x-10)^2 = -(2x-25)(x^2-12x+40)/(x-10)^2 verified exactly; on (0,5) g'>0. Endpoints g(0+)=0, g(5-)=30 confirmed. So g:(0,5)->(0,30) is a strictly increasing bijection.

3. **Theorem (existence/uniqueness):** Follows; brute force over 500 values of n in (0,30) confirms P_n has exactly one real root in (0,5) each time, equal to g^{-1}(n).

4. **Cardano section:** x=t+19/3 gives p=n-61/3, q=3382/27-11n/3 (exact). 108R=4n^3+119n^2-19840n+390000, only real root n=-375/4, complex pair 32+/-4i, so R>0 on [0,30] (390000 at n=0; 9900 at n=30). The real-cube-root argument (A+B, AB=-p/3) is valid. Brute force: the boxed formula reproduces the unique root in (0,5) to 1e-6 for all 500 test n.

5. **Rational/integral propositions:** g(1)=82/9, g(2)=33/2, g(3)=156/7, g(4)=80/3 confirmed, none integral; characterization correct.

6. **Alternative reading:** D=n^2+40n-400, threshold 20(sqrt2-1)=8.284, x_-=0 at n=10, x_-<0 for n>10 — all verified numerically.

**Fix applied:** In the n=15 worked example the text gave a garbled value "q=-83/27·11+...". The correct value is q=1897/27 (=70.259..., positive). Replaced with q=1897/27. The other numerics there (R=1228.47, u_+=-0.0801, u_-=-70.179, x=1.77753) are correct and unchanged.

The proof is now complete and correct.
